entries.h: HTF zone tapped
entries.t:
Chart: 4-hour USD/JPY chart. Price sweeps a low, breaks structure upward (MSS), rallies, then pulls back into the 4H demand zone and reacts.
Slide 1 — 4H chart. Tap to enlarge.
Step 1 · Location and bias
HTF zone tapped
This slide answers the first question of any trade: which direction, and from where?
What happened
Sell-side liquidity was swept. At the bottom left, a horizontal line marks an earlier low. A long wick drives below it and price closes back above. Stops under that low were taken and nobody followed through to the downside.
Structure shifted bullish (MSS). Price then closed above the swing high that had produced the low. On the 4H that turns the bias from bearish to bullish.
A demand zone was left behind. The 4H demand box is drawn around the last consolidation before the candle that broke structure. That is where the buying that changed the trend originated.
Price rallied, then came back. After several days of higher highs, price retraced the whole way down and wicked into the zone for the first time. The final candle on the slide is a strong bullish reaction out of it.
Why this zone is worth trading
It did something. It caused the MSS. Zones that break structure carry more weight than zones that merely paused price.
It is fresh. This is the first return. A zone that has already been tapped has had its orders used.
It is in discount. The zone sits in the lower half of the leg from the swept low to the high. Longs are bought cheap, not chased.
It was born from a sweep. Liquidity grab, then shift, then zone. That order of events is what gives the zone its quality.
Rule to carry forward
Only look for longs when price is inside a fresh HTF demand zone that caused a break of structure and sits in discount. Until price gets there, there is nothing to do. The 4H tap is a reason to watch, not a reason to buy.

entries.h: 30m market shift
entries.t:
Chart: 30-minute USD/JPY chart. Price sells off from a 30m supply zone, breaks a low into the 4H demand zone, then breaks the last lower high (MSS).
Slide 2 — 30m chart. The large olive box is the 4H demand from slide 1.
Step 2 · Confirmation
30m market shift
Dropping to the 30m shows how price arrived at the 4H zone and whether buyers actually showed up. This slide is the “confirmation” in the title.
What happened
The delivery was bearish. From the 30m supply at the top, price made a clean sequence of lower highs and lower lows. Inside the HTF pullback, the 30m trend was down.
30m supply is marked at the origin. It is the base of the sell-off. A dotted line runs from a later high that already wicked up toward it, so buy-side liquidity is resting right at the lower edge of that zone. This becomes the target.
The last low was broken into demand (BoS). The dashed BoS line marks the final 30m low. Price pushes under it and lands inside the 4H demand. On the 30m this looks like bearish continuation. In context, it is a run on sell-side liquidity into a HTF buy zone.
The break failed to continue. There was no follow-through below the BoS. Price reversed from inside the zone.
MSS. A strong bullish leg closed above the last lower high, the high that had produced the final low. The 30m sequence of lower highs is over.
Why this matters
A HTF zone can fail. Buying the first touch means paying for a wide stop below the whole 4H zone and accepting that price may slice straight through. Waiting for the 30m shift costs a few pips of entry price and buys proof that the 4H demand is being defended. It also produces a much tighter stop, which is where the 1:3 comes from.
Rule to carry forward
Inside the HTF zone, wait for three things in this order: a low is taken, price fails to continue lower, and a candle closes above the last lower high with displacement. A wick through the high does not count.
Common mistake
Calling an MSS on a break of a minor internal high. The high that matters is the one that led to the lowest low. On this slide the MSS line starts from that swing, not from the small bounces underneath it.

entries.h: 15m entry
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute USD/JPY chart at the moment of the shift. A 15m order block sits under an imbalance; a long position is planned from the order block to the 30m supply.
Slide 3 — 15m chart at the moment the order is planned. Grey box is risk, blue box is reward.
Step 3 · Refinement and order placement
15m entry
The 30m gave permission. The 15m gives the price. This slide is frozen just after the shift, before the pullback, which is when the limit order is placed.
What is marked
$$$ on the descending line. Each lower high on the way down sits on a trendline. Breakout traders and trailing stops cluster above lines like this, so it is buy-side liquidity and part of what draws price upward.
BoS into 4H demand. The same sweep as slide 2, seen in more detail.
X = liquidity sweep. After the first bounce out of the 4H demand, price dipped once more and a wick ran the small lows left by that bounce, then closed back up. X marks that sweep. It cleared the last sell-side liquidity sitting under price, and the displacement candle followed straight after. The solid line drawn from the sweep's low runs to the bottom of the grey risk box, so that low is also the trade's invalidation.
MSS. One large bullish candle closes through the lower high. That is displacement: speed and range, not a slow grind.
IMB (imbalance). The displacement candle moved so fast that it left a gap in price delivery just above the order block. Price tends to return to rebalance these gaps, which is why a pullback is expected at all.
15m OB. The last bearish candle area before the displacement. It sits directly under the imbalance, so a pullback that fills the IMB arrives at the OB.
Why the entry is here and not elsewhere
The order block is the origin of the move that broke structure. It is inside the 4H demand, below the midpoint of the new bullish leg, and it has an imbalance above it to pull price back. Entry is a buy limit at the top edge of the OB, which is the first price the pullback reaches after filling the imbalance.
The opposing 30m supply is far enough away to pay about three times the risk. If supply had been sitting just above the MSS high, the same pattern would not have been worth taking.
Rule to carry forward
After the MSS, mark the last opposing candle before the displacement. Take it only if it has an imbalance next to it and has not been touched since. Place the limit order immediately; do not chase the breakout candle.

entries.h: Result
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute USD/JPY chart after the trade. Price pulls back into the order block, then rallies through the blue reward box to the 30m supply zone.
Slide 4 — the same 15m chart after the trade played out.
Step 4 · Management and outcome
Result
What happened
Price paused at the MSS high. A few small candles drifted sideways and down. No new low was made.
The imbalance was filled. Price traded back through the IMB.
The OB was tapped by a wick. One candle dipped into the top of the 15m order block and closed back above it. The limit order filled there. Price never came close to the X sweep low.
Expansion. Price rallied in two legs with a shallow pullback between them, taking the highs along the trendline on the way.
Target reached. The top of the blue box is the lower edge of the 30m supply. Price hit it and pushed slightly into the zone.
What to take from it
The fill was shallow. Only a wick entered the OB. An order at the middle or bottom of the OB may not have filled. Entering at the top edge costs a little reward-to-risk and gets you into more trades.
The pullback took time. There were roughly two to three hours on the chart between the shift and the fill. The setup rewards patience with a resting order, not screen-watching.
The target was the zone edge. Taking profit at the first touch of supply meant the trade was closed before any reaction from sellers. What price did afterwards is not shown and is not the trade's concern.
Rule to carry forward
Once filled, do nothing until price either reaches the target or makes a new structural high. Moving the stop early on a 15m wobble is the usual way a 1:3 winner turns into a breakeven.

entries.h: The whole trade in a single picture
entries.t:
Everything as one
The whole trade in a single picture
A schematic of the sequence, not a copy of the chart. Read it left to right.
1 · SWEEP INTO THE ZONE
The 30m downtrend breaks its last low and lands in the fresh 4H demand. Sell stops are taken where higher-timeframe buyers are waiting.
2 · SHIFT
A final liquidity sweep (X) clears the lows under price, and a displacement candle closes above the last lower high. The 30m has turned to agree with the 4H.
3 · ENTRY
The displacement leaves an imbalance above a 15m order block. Price returns, fills the imbalance and taps the top of the OB, where the buy limit is resting.
4 · TARGET
Price expands through the trendline highs to the lower edge of the 30m supply that started the sell-off. The trade closes there at about 3R.
The logic in one sentence
Buy the first pullback after lower-timeframe structure flips inside a higher-timeframe demand zone, risk the low that made the flip, and take profit at the nearest opposing zone.

entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit
entries.t:
Order placement
Entry, stop loss and take profit
Entry
Buy limit at the top edge of the 15m order block.
Place it as soon as the MSS candle closes.
The top edge is where the imbalance ends, so it is the first price a pullback reaches.
In this trade only a wick reached the OB. A deeper order risked no fill.
Add the spread to a buy limit. Buys fill on the ask, which is above the charted price.
Stop loss
Below the low of the X liquidity sweep, plus a small buffer.
The X sweep is the low that launched the MSS. The liquidity there has already been taken, so price has no reason to return. If it does break, the bullish shift is void and the reason for the trade is gone.
This is lower than the bottom of the OB. A stop tucked just under the OB is exposed to a slightly deeper wick.
Buffer: a few pips below the wick. Sell stops trigger on the bid, so the spread does not need to be added on a long.
More conservative: below the sweep low inside the 4H zone. Safer, and it lowers the reward-to-risk.
Take profit
Lower edge of the 30m supply. About 3R.
It is the first opposing zone, and the origin of the sell-off. Sellers may be waiting there.
The trendline highs ($$$) and the earlier high near the zone edge are liquidity that pulls price up to it.
The target is the near edge, not inside the zone. Do not ask price to push through sellers to pay you.
Set the order a touch below the edge. Price often turns a few pips short of a zone.
Managing the position
The post shows a single entry and a single exit. The points below are my suggested handling, not something marked on the slides.
Leave the stop alone until price closes above the MSS high and prints a new 15m higher low. Then it can trail to just under that higher low.
Optional partial at the MSS high or at the trendline liquidity if you want to pay yourself early. Decide this before entry, not during.
Cancel the limit if price reaches about half of the way to target without filling you. The reward that justified the trade is no longer there.
Position size
Fix the money at risk first, then let the stop distance decide the lot size.
Lots = money at risk ÷ (stop in pips × pip value per lot)
On USD/JPY one standard lot moves ¥1,000 per pip. In dollars that is 1,000 ÷ the USD/JPY rate, for example about $6.67 at 150.00.
Example: $10,000 account, 1% risk = $100. Stop of 15 pips at $6.67 per pip per lot gives 100 ÷ (15 × 6.67) ≈ 1.0 lot. At 1:3 the target pays about $300.

entries.h: Step-by-step for the next trade
entries.t:
Repeatable strategy
Step-by-step for the next trade
Work down the list in order. Each step is a yes or no. A “no” ends the process for that pair. For shorts, mirror everything: supply for demand, highs for lows.
Mark the 4H structure and its zones.Find the last break of structure. Mark the demand zone that caused it. Check it is untouched and in the lower half of the leg.
Wait for price to enter the zone.Set an alert at the top edge. No alert, no analysis.
Drop to the 30m and map the way in.Mark the lower highs and lower lows of the pullback, the last low, and the supply zone at its origin. That supply is your likely target.
Did price take a low inside the zone?You want the last 30m low run while price is in HTF demand. No sweep means the liquidity is still below you.
Did a candle close above the last lower high with displacement?This is the MSS. It must be a close, from a large-bodied candle, through the high that produced the lowest low.
On the 15m, is there an order block with an imbalance beside it?Mark the last bearish candle before the displacement. It should be unmitigated and sit inside the HTF zone.
Does the trade pay at least 1:2 to the first opposing zone?Measure entry at the OB top, stop under the sweep low that launched the MSS, target at the near edge of supply. Under 1:2, skip it.
Place the orders.Buy limit, stop loss and take profit together. Size the position for a fixed risk of 0.5–1% of the account.
Manage by structure, then record it.Hold until target, stop, or a new structural high lets you trail. Screenshot the 4H, 30m and 15m and log the result, win or lose.

entries.h: When this setup should be skipped
entries.t:
Filters
When this setup should be skipped
Do not take it if
The 4H zone has already been tapped and reacted once.
Price closes a 4H candle below the bottom of the demand zone.
The “shift” is a wick through the high, or a slow overlapping crawl with no imbalance.
The opposing supply is so close that the trade pays less than 1:2.
Price runs to target without pulling back. The trade is missed, not chased.
High-impact news for USD or JPY is due before the pullback is likely to fill.
This trade had all of these
Fresh 4H demand that caused a 4H MSS, in discount.
Sell-side liquidity taken on the way into the zone.
30m MSS on a single displacement candle.
Imbalance sitting directly on a 15m order block.
A second liquidity sweep (X) just before the shift, giving a clear low for the stop.
Unmitigated 30m supply about 3R away, with trendline liquidity along the path.
Keep this in proportion
This is one trade, chosen for a post because it worked. The same pattern also loses: the zone fails, the order block is run, or price never pulls back. What makes it a strategy is taking every valid occurrence with the same risk and counting the results. Collect at least 50 examples in backtesting, losers included, before trusting the numbers.

entries.p: USD/JPY Weekly, Daily and 4H Swing Long
entries.h: Weekly: the 2024 high is broken
entries.t:
Chart: Weekly USD/JPY chart from 2024 to 2026. A line marked bos runs from the July 2024 high near 162 to mid-2026, where price closes above it and reaches about 164. Price then falls to about 153 and bounces to 156.85.
Screenshot 1 — Weekly. The July 2024 high is broken in 2026.
Step 1 · Weekly bias
Weekly: the 2024 high is broken
What the chart shows
The old high. July 2024, just under 162. Price fell from it to about 140 and spent almost two years below it.
BoS. In mid-2026 weekly candles close above that high and reach about 164.
The pullback. Price drops back fast to about 153, then starts to bounce. It is at 156.85 on this screenshot.
Why it matters
A weekly break of a two-year high sets the direction: longs. The fall afterwards is large in pips, but on the weekly it is a pullback after a break. The weekly does not say where the pullback ends, so the next chart has to.
Rule to carry forward
Take the direction from the highest timeframe that has just broken structure. Then look for a zone on the next timeframe down. Do not buy only because the weekly is bullish.

entries.p: USD/JPY Weekly, Daily and 4H Swing Long
entries.h: Daily: back to the demand that started the rally
entries.t:
Chart: Daily USD/JPY chart from October 2025. A red line marked X sits under a December low near 154.3, which is swept in late January. A line marked MSS at about 159.45 is broken in March. A grey demand zone from about 152.7 to 153.9 starts in mid-February. Price rallies to 164, falls sharply, and returns into the zone in September.
Screenshot 2 — Daily. The demand zone that started the rally, revisited seven months later.
Step 2 · Daily zone
Daily: back to the demand that started the rally
What the chart shows
The sweep (X). A December 2025 low near 154.3 is taken in late January. Price drops to about 152.1.
MSS. Price then closes above the January high near 159.45. That is the daily shift up.
The demand zone. Drawn at the February low the shift came from, about 152.7 to 153.9.
The return. After the top near 164, price falls about 1,100 pips and reaches the zone in September. The low is about 152.9, inside it.
Why it matters
This is the location. The zone came after a sweep, it produced a break of structure, and price had not returned to it since February. That is a fresh zone by the rules on the supply and demand page.
One detail: the January sweep low near 152.1 sits below the zone. If the zone had failed, that low was the next level down.
Rule to carry forward
A daily zone is a place to start watching. Nothing is bought here yet.

entries.p: USD/JPY Weekly, Daily and 4H Swing Long
entries.h: Daily: a break down, a supply zone, then a shift up
entries.t:
Chart: Daily chart, 2026. After the high near 164, a line marked bos at about 155.2 under the early August low is broken in September. A grey supply zone from about 159.6 to 160.4 is drawn at the high before that break. Price bounces from the demand zone and a small line marked MSS at about 156.75 is broken.
Screenshot 3 — Daily. A break down, the supply it leaves, and the shift back up.
Step 3 · Daily shift
Daily: a break down, a supply zone, then a shift up
What the chart shows
BoS down. The early August low near 155.2 is broken in September. For a while the daily is bearish.
Supply. The high the break came from, about 159.6 to 160.4, is marked as a supply zone.
Reaction at demand. Price spends several days inside the February demand zone without closing below it.
MSS up. Price closes above the last lower high near 156.75, with a wick to about 158.
Why it matters
Two things are settled here. The daily demand held and the daily has turned back up, so the weekly direction and the daily now agree. And the trade has a ceiling: a fresh daily supply zone at 159.6. A long from below should be closed there.
Mark the opposing zone before the entry
The supply zone was drawn weeks before the trade. The target was known first, and the entry had to pay enough to reach it.

entries.p: USD/JPY Weekly, Daily and 4H Swing Long
entries.h: Daily: the shift leaves a new demand zone
entries.t:
Chart: Daily chart from July to September 2026. Price falls from 164 through the bos line into the lower demand zone, rallies, and breaks the MSS line at about 156.75. A new grey demand zone is drawn from about 155.3 to 156.3 at the base of the last push.
Screenshot 4 — Daily, closer. The new demand zone left by the shift.
Step 4 · The zone to trade from
Daily: the shift leaves a new demand zone
What the chart shows
The rally from demand. A run of up candles from about 153 to 158.
The new zone. About 155.3 to 156.3, at the base of the push that broke the MSS line.
Price now. Above the zone at 156.85, with a long upper wick.
Why it matters
Price is too far from the February zone to buy there with a sensible stop. The new zone is the place to wait for a pullback. It is closer to the target, so the stop has to be small, and that needs the 4H.

entries.p: USD/JPY Weekly, Daily and 4H Swing Long
entries.h: 4H: the shift, seen up close
entries.t:
Chart: 4-hour chart, August to September 2026. Price falls from the supply zone near 160 through the bos line. A small low marked X near 155.3 and a high near 156.75 form on the way down. Price bottoms in the demand zone near 153, rallies, and breaks the MSS line at 156.75, reaching 158. The new demand zone from 155.3 to 156.3 is marked.
Screenshot 5 — 4H. The same shift, seen on the entry timeframe.
Step 5 · 4H structure
4H: the shift, seen up close
What the chart shows
The drop. From the supply zone near 160 to the daily demand near 153 in about a week.
A pause on the way. A low near 155.3 (marked X) and a bounce to 156.75. That bounce high is the level the MSS line is drawn from.
The base. Several days of lows around 153 inside the daily demand zone.
MSS. Price climbs back and closes above 156.75, reaching about 158.
Why it matters
The 4H agrees with the daily. The demand zone at 155.3 to 156.3 is now the area to watch, and the plan is to wait for price to come back to it.

entries.p: USD/JPY Weekly, Daily and 4H Swing Long
entries.h: 4H: a month of range, then price reaches the zone
entries.t:
Chart: 4-hour chart, September to October 2026. After the MSS, price ranges between about 156.4 and 159 for a month. In late October it drops, wicks to about 156.1 into the top of the demand zone, and bounces to 157.27. A small MSS line is marked at about 157.35.
Screenshot 6 — 4H. A month of range, then the drop into the zone.
Step 6 · The wait
4H: a month of range, then price reaches the zone
What the chart shows
The range. From about 20 September to 21 October price moves between roughly 156.4 and 159. It does not reach the demand zone and does not reach the supply zone.
The drop. Around 21–22 October price falls out of the range and wicks to about 156.1, into the top of the zone.
The level to beat. A small MSS line at about 157.35, the last lower high of the drop.
Why it matters
About a month passed between the shift and this return. There was no trade in that time, because price was in the middle with the zone below and the supply above. The lows of the range, just above the zone, were building up stops the whole time.
Rule to carry forward
No trade in the middle of a range. Wait for price to reach the zone.

entries.p: USD/JPY Weekly, Daily and 4H Swing Long
entries.h: 4H: the range low is swept, then the shift
entries.t:
Chart: 4-hour chart, zoomed in. A red line marked X runs under the range low of late September at about 156.38. A wick on about 22 October dips below it to about 156.07, into the top of the demand zone. Price then rises and closes above the MSS line at about 157.35. A small demand zone from about 156.65 to 157.15 is drawn at the base of that move.
Screenshot 7 — 4H. The range low is swept into the zone, then the 4H shifts up.
Step 7 · Sweep and shift
4H: the range low is swept, then the shift
What the chart shows
The liquidity. The range low of about 29–30 September, near 156.38. Three weeks of trading sat above it.
The sweep (X). A wick to about 156.07 takes that low and reaches the top of the demand zone. The candles close back above the line.
MSS. Price closes above 157.35.
The entry zone. A small 4H demand zone at about 156.65 to 157.15, the base of the move that made the shift.
Why it matters
This is the confirmation. The sweep happened at the zone, not above it, and the shift followed straight after. The small zone gives an entry with a stop of about 110 pips. An entry at the larger zone would have needed a stop of about 200.
Rule to carry forward
At the zone, wait for a low to be swept and for a close above the last lower high. Then use the small zone that move leaves.

entries.p: USD/JPY Weekly, Daily and 4H Swing Long
entries.h: 4H: entry, stop and target
entries.t:
Chart: 4-hour chart with a long position drawn. Entry at 157.156 at the top of the small demand zone, stop at 156.069 just under the sweep wick, target at 159.599 at the bottom edge of the daily supply zone.
Screenshot 8 — 4H. The order: entry 157.156, stop 156.069, target 159.599.
Step 8 · The order
4H: entry, stop and target
What the chart shows
Entry: buy limit at 157.156, the top edge of the small 4H demand zone.
Stop loss: 156.069, under the sweep wick. That is about 109 pips.
Take profit: 159.599, the bottom edge of the daily supply zone. That is about 244 pips.
Reward to risk: about 1:2.25.
Why each level is where it is
The entry is the near edge of the zone, where the other trades on this site were filled. The stop is beyond the sweep low: if price goes back under 156.07, the sweep was a real break and the idea is wrong. The target is the first opposing zone, marked on the daily before the trade existed.
The buffer is thin
The sweep wick is at about 156.07 and the stop at 156.069. That leaves about a pip. Spread alone can be more than that. A buffer of 5 to 10 pips puts the stop near 156.00 and the ratio at about 1:2.1.

entries.p: USD/JPY Weekly, Daily and 4H Swing Long
entries.h: 4H: filled at the edge, target reached
entries.t:
Chart: 4-hour chart showing the result. Price pulls back to the entry at 157.144 with a wick slightly below it, ranges between about 157.3 and 158.8, then rallies to the target at 159.587 and on into the supply zone to about 160.05.
Screenshot 9 — 4H. Filled at the edge, target reached. The box now reads 157.144, 156.057 and 159.587.
Step 9 · Result
4H: filled at the edge, target reached
What the chart shows
The fill. Price comes back to the zone a few days after the shift. The wick goes about 10 pips past the entry and turns.
The hold. Roughly a week of sideways trading between 157.3 and 158.8. Price never came near the stop.
The target. A strong push reaches 159.587 and continues into the supply zone, to about 160.05.
What to take from it
The fill only just reached the zone. A limit in the middle of it would have been missed.
The trade took about two weeks from fill to target. This is a swing trade and it has to be sized and left alone like one.
Price went straight into the supply zone after the target. Closing at the bottom edge was the plan, and what the zone does next is a separate trade.
The dates after 27 October are hidden by the toolbar. I estimate the shift at about 26 October, the fill at about 30 October and the target at about 10–11 November, from the spacing of the candles.

entries.p: USD/JPY Weekly, Daily and 4H Swing Long
entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit
entries.t:
Order placement
Entry, stop loss and take profit
Entry
Buy limit at 157.144, the top edge of the small 4H demand zone.
The zone is the base of the move that closed above 157.35.
Place the order when that 4H candle has closed.
The fill went about 10 pips past the edge. A deeper order would have missed.
Stop loss
156.057, under the sweep wick. About 109 pips.
Under 156.07 the sweep has become a break, and the reason for the trade is gone.
The buffer here is about a pip. Use 5 to 10 pips plus the spread.
The wider choice is under the 155.3–156.3 zone. That is about 190 pips and brings the ratio to about 1:1.3, which is too low.
Take profit
159.587, the bottom edge of the daily supply zone. About 244 pips.
The first opposing zone above the entry, and a fresh one.
The range highs near 159 sit just under it. They are taken on the way.
The order is a pip or two under the zone edge, so the zone does not have to be entered.
Position size with a 109-pip stop
On USD/JPY one standard lot moves ¥1,000 per pip, about $6.36 at 157.14. A 109-pip stop therefore costs about $693 per lot. To risk 1% of a $1,000 account ($10) the size is 10 ÷ 693 ≈ 0.014, so 0.01 lots, which risks about $6.90. On a $10,000 account, 1% is about 0.14 lots. A swing stop means a small position. Do not shrink the stop to fit a bigger one.

entries.p: USD/JPY Weekly, Daily and 4H Swing Long
entries.h: What was done well, and what to tighten
entries.t:
Review
What was done well, and what to tighten
Done well
Direction came from the weekly, and the daily had to agree before anything was planned.
The target zone was marked on the daily weeks before the entry.
A month of range was sat out. No order was placed in the middle.
The entry waited for a sweep at the zone and a shift after it.
The stop is behind the sweep, where the idea is wrong, and the target is the first opposing zone.
To tighten
Stop buffer. About a pip under the wick. Add 5 to 10 pips plus spread.
Ratio. About 1:2.25 is the lowest on this site, and about 1:2.1 with a proper buffer. It passes the 1:2 rule with little to spare. At 1:2.25 you need to win about 31% of the time to break even, before costs.
The daily had broken down. Between early and mid-September the daily was bearish under the 155.2 break. The trade was only valid after the daily MSS. Keep that as a written condition.
Swap. A two-week hold pays or earns overnight interest. Check the rate on your broker and include it in the journal.
Replay. Draw the zones before stepping the chart forward, and record the trades that lose as well. One win says the method can work once.

entries.p: USD/JPY Weekly, Daily and 4H Swing Long
entries.h: Step-by-step for the next trade
entries.t:
Repeatable strategy
Step-by-step for the next trade
Written for longs. For shorts, mirror it. A “no” at any step ends the process.
Weekly: has price just closed beyond a major high?Write “long”. If the weekly is inside a range, use the daily for direction and halve the size.
Daily: is price pulling back into a fresh demand zone that produced a break?Mark it. Mark the nearest supply zone above as the target.
Daily: has price reacted and closed above its last lower high?Draw the new demand zone at the base of that move.
Is price back at that zone?If it is ranging above it, wait. Set an alert at the top edge.
4H: has a low been swept into the zone, with a close back above?Mark the sweep low.
4H: has a candle closed above the last lower high?Draw the small zone at the base of that move.
Buy limit at the top of the small zone, stop under the sweep low plus 5–10 pips.Target the bottom edge of the daily supply.
Does it pay at least 1:2 with the buffer included?If not, skip it.
Size for the wide stop, place, hold, record.Risk 0.5–1%. Expect to hold for days or weeks. Screenshot the weekly, daily and 4H.

entries.p: USD/JPY Weekly, Daily and 4H Swing Long
entries.h: When this setup should be skipped
entries.t:
Filters
When this setup should be skipped
Do not take it if
A daily candle closes below the daily demand zone.
The daily has not closed back above its last lower high.
Price is in the middle of the range, between the demand and the supply.
The 4H breaks up without first sweeping a low at the zone.
The daily supply is closer than 1:2 from the entry.
A Bank of Japan or Federal Reserve decision, or US jobs or inflation data, is due before the order is likely to fill.
The position needed for the stop is below your broker’s minimum size at the risk you allow.
This trade had all of these
A weekly break of structure upward.
A fresh daily demand zone that held.
A daily shift up and a marked supply zone above.
A swept range low at the zone.
A 4H shift and a small zone to enter from.
A target about 2.25R away.
Keep this in proportion
USD/JPY at these levels has a history of sudden moves of several hundred pips in a day, and the fall from 164 on these charts is one of them. A stop order can be filled well beyond its price in a move like that. Keep the risk per trade small enough that a slipped stop is survivable.

Case study · Volatility 75 (1s) · Your own replay
15m Supply Short, Two Entries
Five screenshots from your replay of one morning on the Volatility 75 (1s) index. A 15m low breaks, and the protected swing and the supply zone are marked. Price returns to the zone and a first short is placed at its edge. Price then sweeps a high inside the zone and shifts down, which gives a second, confirmed short. Both reach the target at the low.

Everything as one
Entry, SL & TP

When to skip
How to read this page
These are your screenshots in TradingView replay mode, in the order you sent them, with your own marks: bos, MSS, X for a level that was swept, $$$ for liquidity, Protected swing, grey boxes for supply and a teal box for demand. You sent no notes, so the reasoning is my reading. Order prices are those printed on the price axis; other prices are approximate. The position size is not shown.
A synthetic index is not a market
Volatility 75 (1s) prices are generated by the provider, not by buyers and sellers, so sweeps and zones here cannot have the causes this site describes, and random prices draw them too. The first Volatility 75 case explains this in full. Treat this page as practice in the routine, and keep its result out of your statistics for real markets.

entries.h: A low breaks: mark the protected swing and the zone
entries.t:
Chart: Fifteen-minute chart of the Volatility 75 (1s) index in replay. Price makes lower highs marked X and breaks lows marked bos and MSS. A final high near 4,086 is marked Protected swing with a grey supply zone below it from about 4,062 to 4,085. Price has fallen from the zone and broken the low marked bos, and is at 4,028. A teal zone sits at the bottom of the chart.
Screenshot 1 — 15m, replay. The low has just broken; the protected swing and the zone are marked.
Step 1 · Structure
A low breaks: mark the protected swing and the zone
What the chart shows
X marks. Earlier highs that were taken, each followed by a lower low.
bos, MSS, bos. The 15m is making lower lows. The last bos, near 4,034, has just been closed below.
Protected swing, about 4,087. The high that the breaking move came from.
The grey box, about 4,062 to 4,085. The last up candles before that fall: the supply zone.
The teal zone at the bottom. A higher-timeframe demand area, below about 3,965.
Why it matters
The moment the low breaks, three things are fixed: the direction (short), the level that proves the idea wrong (the protected swing) and the place to sell from (the supply that caused the break). Nothing is traded yet. Price is at 4,028, well below the zone, and selling here would mean a stop of almost 60 points.
Rule to carry forward
When a low breaks, mark the protected swing and the supply zone straight away. Then wait for price to come back to the zone.

entries.h: Mark the target, then let price return
entries.t:
Chart: The same chart several hours later. Price fell to a low near 3,966, where a red line marked with dollar signs is drawn above the teal zone. Price then rallied back into the grey supply zone, reaching about 4,078, dropped to about 4,025 and has returned to the bottom edge of the zone at 4,064.
Screenshot 2 — 15m, replay. The low is marked as the target; price is back at the zone.
Step 2 · Target and return
Mark the target, then let price return
What the chart shows
The fall. From the zone price drops to about 3,966.
$$$ at about 3,965. The line under that low. Stops rest below it, and it sits on the top edge of the teal demand zone.
The rally. Price climbs back about 110 points into the supply zone and reaches about 4,078.
The first reaction. It drops to about 4,025, then comes back to the bottom edge of the zone at 4,064.
Why it matters
The target is chosen before the entry: the low, which is both liquidity and the edge of the opposing zone. The rally is large, but the protected swing at 4,087 has not been touched, so the short idea is intact.
Note that the zone has now been entered once. The entry in the next step is on the second approach. A zone is strongest on its first touch.
Rule to carry forward
A deep pullback does not cancel the idea. A close beyond the protected swing does.

entries.h: Sell at the bottom edge of the zone
entries.t:
Chart: The same chart with a short position drawn. The entry is 4,062.63 at the bottom edge of the supply zone, the stop is 4,088.52 above the protected swing line, and the target is 3,965.15 at the line marked with dollar signs.
Screenshot 3 — 15m, replay. The first sell: entry 4,062.63, stop 4,088.52, target 3,965.15.
Step 3 · First order
Sell at the bottom edge of the zone
What the chart shows
Entry 4,062.63. The bottom edge of the supply.
Stop 4,088.52. About a point and a half above the protected swing.
Target 3,965.15. On the $$$ line, at the top of the teal zone.
The numbers. About 26 points of risk for about 97 of reward, roughly 1:3.8.
Why it matters
All three orders come from marks made earlier. The stop is beyond the protected swing, so it is only hit if the idea is wrong. The target is the first opposing level.
This entry has no shift behind it. Price reacted from the zone once but did not break a 15m low before this sell, so it is an entry on the touch.
Rule to carry forward
Entry at the near edge of the zone, stop beyond the protected swing, target at the first opposing liquidity. If the three do not give 1:2, skip it.

entries.h: A sweep and a shift give a second entry
entries.t:
Chart: The same chart two hours later. After the first entry, price pushed up to about 4,078, taking a high marked X, then fell through a low marked MSS near 4,023 to about 3,978 and bounced to 4,016. A new supply zone is drawn from about 4,058 to 4,086 with a second short position: entry 4,058.67, stop 4,086.94, target 3,967.27.
Screenshot 4 — 15m, replay. A high is swept, structure shifts down, and a second sell is planned at 4,058.67.
Step 4 · Second setup
A sweep and a shift give a second entry
What the chart shows
X near 4,078. After the first entry, price pushes up again and takes the high of the first reaction. The first trade is about 15 points against at this moment.
MSS near 4,023. Price then falls and closes below the low of the reaction. The 15m has shifted down from inside the zone.
The fall stops at about 3,978, some 13 points short of the target, and price bounces.
A new grey box, about 4,058 to 4,086. The supply left by the move that made the shift.
Second sell. Entry 4,058.67, stop 4,086.94, target 3,967.27. About 28 points of risk for 91 of reward, roughly 1:3.2.
Why it matters
This is the full sequence from the notes, mirrored for a short: a sweep of a high inside the zone, a shift down, then a sell at the supply that caused the shift. The first entry was taken on the touch. This one has confirmation.
The first trade came within 13 points of its target and then gave most of it back. Nothing in the plan said to close early, so it stays open.
Rule to carry forward
The strongest entry is the one after a sweep and a shift inside the zone. If you take only one of the two entries, take this one.
Two positions, one idea
If the first short is still open when the second fills, both stops are near 4,087 and both can be hit together. For risk, that is one trade of double size. The scaling rules say to size the two so that together they stay within your limit for one trade, for example half the normal risk on each.

entries.h: The second sell fills and both targets are reached
entries.t:
Chart: The finished chart. Price rallied from about 3,978 back up to about 4,060, touching the second entry, then fell in a few candles through the target line near 3,966 and into the teal zone to about 3,930.
Screenshot 5 — 15m. The second sell is filled at the zone edge and both targets are reached.
Step 5 · Result
The second sell fills and both targets are reached
What the chart shows
The rally. Price climbs from about 3,978 back to about 4,060 and touches the second entry at 4,058.67.
The first trade is back within 3 points of its own entry at this moment, after being about 85 points in profit.
The fall. Price drops through 4,000 and through the $$$ line. Both targets, 3,967.27 and 3,965.15, are reached.
After the target. Price continues into the teal zone to about 3,930.
Why it matters
The second entry filled by a point or two. An order placed deeper in the zone would have been missed.
Price went another 35 points past the targets. That is not a mistake in the plan: the target was the top of a demand zone, and the plan was to be out before it.
Rule to carry forward
Take the profit at the level you marked. What price does after the target is not part of the trade.

entries.h: Everything as one
entries.t:
Bringing it together
Everything as one
1 · BREAK
A 15m low breaks. Direction: short. The high the move came from is the protected swing.
2 · ZONE
The last up candles before the fall are the supply zone, about 4,062–4,085.
3 · TARGET
The low near 3,965, with stops beneath it and a demand zone under that.
4 · FIRST ENTRY
Price returns. Sell at the zone edge, stop above the protected swing. No shift yet.
5 · SWEEP AND SHIFT
A high inside the zone is taken and a 15m low breaks. A second sell is placed at the new supply.
6 · RESULT
Price returns once more, fills the second sell and falls to both targets.

entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit
entries.t:
Order placement
Entry, stop loss and take profit
Entry
Sell limits at the bottom edge of the supply: 4,062.63, then 4,058.67.
Both are at the first price where the zone can react.
The first is on the return to the zone. The second follows a sweep and a shift.
The second filled by a point or two.
Stop loss
4,088.52 for the first, 4,086.94 for the second. About 26 and 28 points.
The first stop is above the protected swing at about 4,087. That is the right side of it.
The second is a fraction below that line. Put it above the swing as well, with a few points of buffer and the spread.
The highest price after the first entry was about 4,078, some 10 points under the stops.
Take profit
3,965.15 and 3,967.27, at the low above the demand zone. About 97 and 91 points.
The low is liquidity and the edge of the first opposing zone.
The second target, two points higher, is the better placement: a short closes at the buy price, which is above the chart price.
Price went about 35 points further. The plan was to be out before the demand.
Position size
Size = money at risk ÷ (stop in points × value of one point per lot), using the point value and smallest lot from your platform’s contract specification. With two entries on one idea, divide the risk between them. For a 1% limit, that is 0.5% on each: with a 26-point stop and, as an example only, $1 per point per lot, 0.5% of $1,000 is 5 ÷ 26 ≈ 0.19 lots.

entries.h: What was done well and what to tighten
entries.t:
Review
What was done well and what to tighten
Done well
The protected swing, the zone and the target were all marked before any order.
Both entries were at the zone edge, not in the middle of the move.
The first stop was beyond the protected swing.
The second entry waited for a sweep and a shift.
The first trade was held through a return to its entry, and was not closed early when it stalled near the target.
Reward to risk was above 1:3 on both.
To tighten
The first entry was on the zone’s second approach and had no shift. Record it as an aggressive entry.
The second stop sits just under the protected swing. Move it above.
No higher timeframe is shown. Check the 1H direction and what the teal zone is before selling into it.
Decide the combined risk before the second order, and write it down.
The first trade gave back about 85 points of open profit before winning. Decide in advance whether you hold for the full target every time, and keep to it.
Compared with your trade the day before
In the 1H case the sell was also at the zone edge, but with no protected swing marked and a thin buffer. Here the swing is named, the stops are tied to it and the second entry is confirmed. That is progress in the routine, which is the part you control.

entries.h: The steps for the next one
entries.t:
Repeatable
The steps for the next one
Has a low just broken with a candle close?Yes. Direction: short.
Where is the protected swing?The high the breaking move came from. Marked.
Where is the supply?The last up candles before the fall. Marked and extended right.
Where is the target?The low just made, or the top of the demand under it. At least 1:2 from the zone edge.
Has price returned to the zone?Wait. Do not sell in between.
Sweep and shift inside the zone?Best case: a high is taken and a low breaks. Sell at the supply that caused the shift.
Orders?Sell limit at the bottom edge. Stop above the protected swing plus buffer and spread. Target a little above the low.
Second entry on the same idea?Only with a new setup, and with the combined risk inside one trade’s limit.
What cancels it?A candle close above the protected swing.

entries.h: When this setup should be skipped
entries.t:
Filters
When this setup should be skipped
Do not take it if
A candle has closed above the protected swing.
The zone has already been used several times.
The low is closer than 1:2 from the entry.
The higher timeframe has just broken upward, or price is rising out of a higher-timeframe demand.
A second entry would take the combined risk over your limit.
This trade had all of these
A series of 15m lower lows.
A marked protected swing that was never broken.
A supply zone at the start of the breaking move.
A target at clear liquidity, more than 1:3 away.
For the second entry, a sweep and a shift inside the zone.
Keep this in proportion
These are two winning trades on one idea, in replay, on a synthetic index. They show the routine being followed more carefully than before. They do not show that it makes money. Keep logging until you have fifty setups, losses and skipped trades included, and run the same routine on a real market in replay.

How to read this page
You sent one screenshot and no notes, so the reasoning is my reading of what you drew: bos, MSS, X for a level that was swept, grey boxes for zones and the position boxes. Order prices are the ones printed on the price axis. Other prices are read from the axis and are approximate. The chart is on a paper-trading account, so no money was at risk.

entries.h: synthetic
entries.t:
Read this first: a synthetic index is not a market
Volatility 75 (1s) is one of Deriv’s synthetic indices. Its price is produced by the provider’s random number generator with a fixed volatility of 75% a year, one tick every second. No buyers, sellers or banks are behind it, and no stop orders move it.
The reasons this site gives for a sweep or a zone (stops being collected, unfilled orders waiting) cannot be what moves this chart.
Random prices also draw sweeps, breaks and zones. A setup that works here once, or several times, is not evidence of an edge.
A volatility of 75% a year is roughly 4% a day, about 160 points at this price. The 55-point stop on this trade is about a third of one ordinary day’s movement.
The page is still useful as practice in marking structure, placing the three orders and holding a trade. Keep its result out of the statistics for your forex, gold and Bitcoin trades, and backtest this index separately before risking money on it.

entries.h: chart
entries.t:
Chart: One-hour chart of the Volatility 75 (1s) index over about four days. Price falls and breaks two lows marked bos. A grey supply zone sits from about 4,294 to 4,347 above them. Price returns to the zone two days later, where a short position is drawn with entry 4,294.29, stop 4,349.84 and a target near 4,017. Price falls, rallies back to about 4,322, then falls to a grey demand zone near 4,015. Three smaller short positions are drawn on the way down.
Your screenshot — Volatility 75 (1s), 1H, Deriv feed, four days. Select it to enlarge.

entries.h: A high is swept, then two lows break
entries.t:
Step 1 · Left of the chart
A high is swept, then two lows break
What the chart shows
X near 4,328. A high from earlier on the first day. One tall candle trades above it to about 4,347 and the next candle falls back below.
Two bos lines. Price then drops fast and closes below two earlier lows, near 4,203 and near 4,160.
The low. The fall ends near 4,050 early on the second day.
Why it matters
This is the order from the trading notes, mirrored for a short: a sweep first, then the break. The two breaks set the direction to short. The high of the sweep, about 4,347, becomes the protected high.
Rule to carry forward
For shorts, the break of a low should follow a sweep of a high. The top of that sweep is the protected high, and the stop goes above it.

entries.h: Mark the supply that broke the lows
entries.t:
Step 2 · The zone
Mark the supply that broke the lows
What the chart shows
The grey box at the top. About 4,294 to 4,347. It covers the last up candle before the fall, including the sweep wick.
It is extended to the right until price comes back to it.
The grey box at the bottom. A demand zone from about 3,980 to 4,015. This is the target area.
Why it matters
The zone is the start of the move that broke structure, and it has not been revisited. The demand below is the first opposing zone, so it is where the trade should end. Both are marked before price returns, which is what makes the trade a plan.
Rule to carry forward
Mark the entry zone and the target zone as soon as the break happens. If the distance between them is less than twice the height of the stop, there is no trade.

entries.h: Price climbs back and takes a high on the way
entries.t:
Step 3 · The return
Price climbs back and takes a high on the way
What the chart shows
The long X line near 4,282. It marks the lower high left just after the fall began.
The rally. From about 4,050, price climbs for roughly a day.
The line is crossed early on the third day, and price continues into the supply zone a few points above.
Why it matters
That lower high sat just under the zone. On a traded market it would be inducement: sellers who shorted early have stops above it, and those are taken before the real zone is reached. Selling at 4,282 would have meant a stop inside the supply zone.
Rule to carry forward
When a clear high sits just in front of your supply, expect it to be taken first. Keep the order at the zone, not at the high.

entries.h: Sell at the bottom edge of the zone
entries.t:
Step 4 · The order
Sell at the bottom edge of the zone
What the chart shows
Entry 4,294.29. The bottom edge of the supply.
Stop 4,349.84. About 3 points above the top of the zone and the sweep high.
Target near 4,017 to 4,020. Just above the demand zone.
The fill. Price trades up to about 4,325 inside the zone, then turns down.
Why it matters
The order is at the first price where the zone can react. Price went about 31 points past it, a little over half of the stop distance, before falling. A stop inside the zone would have been hit.
This is an entry without a lower-timeframe shift
The chart shows no 15m or 5m shift before this entry. If there was none, this is an aggressive entry: a limit order at the zone, taken on the touch. The other twelve cases on this site waited for a shift. See entry models for the difference. If you did confirm on a lower timeframe, send that chart and I will add it.

entries.h: Price comes all the way back, and the stop holds
entries.t:
Step 5 · The hold
Price comes all the way back, and the stop holds
What the chart shows
The first fall. Price drops to about 4,068 by the evening of the third day, roughly 225 points in profit.
The rally. Early on the fourth day, three tall candles take price back to about 4,322. That is 28 points above the entry.
X near 4,296. A small high from the first fall is taken by that rally.
The MSS line near 4,323. The top of the rally. A close above it would have turned the 1H upward. Price did not close above it.
The stop at 4,349.84 was about 28 points away at the worst moment.
Why it matters
This is the hardest part of the trade. A stop moved to the entry price after the first fall would have closed the trade for nothing, hours before the target was reached. The original stop was beyond the protected high, and the protected high was never broken, so the idea was still valid.
Rule to carry forward
The trade is wrong when the protected high breaks, not when price returns to your entry. Decide before entering whether you will move the stop, and at what point. Then follow that.

entries.h: A new supply zone, and three smaller shorts
entries.t:
Step 6 · Fourth day
A new supply zone, and three smaller shorts
What the chart shows
MSS near 4,125. After the rally fails, price closes below the low it started from. The 1H is pointing down again.
A new grey box, about 4,201 to 4,240. The supply left by that fall, with the prices 4,201.57 and 4,244.72 beside it. These look like a second sell order and its stop. Price did not return to it, so it was not filled.
Three small position boxes lower down, each beside small X and MSS marks. Reading the axis labels, they are roughly: sell 4,108 with stop 4,138; sell 4,099 with stop 4,116; sell 4,077 with stop 4,096.
All targets are together between 4,014 and 4,020.
Why it matters
Each small short repeats the same sequence at a smaller size: a small high is taken, structure shifts down, and a sell is placed at the small supply. Adding in the direction of a trade that is already working is a reasonable way to build a position. It also adds risk each time.
Count the total risk
Four open shorts on one idea are one trade for risk purposes. If each one risks 1%, a sharp move against you costs 4%. Keep the total within your limit for one trade, for example by risking 0.25–0.5% on each addition, or by adding only after the stop on the earlier position has been moved to lock in profit.
The pairing of entry and stop prices for the three small shorts is my reading of the labels at this zoom, and may be slightly off.

entries.h: Target reached at the demand zone
entries.t:
Step 7 · Result
Target reached at the demand zone
What the chart shows
The last fall. Late on the fourth day price drops through 4,040 into the demand zone.
The targets near 4,017 are reached. The low is about 3,975, at the bottom of the zone.
The bounce. Price turns up from the zone and is at about 4,062 when the screenshot is taken.
Why it matters
The target was just above the demand zone, not inside it. Price did go deeper, but the bounce began within a few candles. Taking profit before the opposing zone is what the plan said, and it kept the result.

entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit
entries.t:
Order placement
Entry, stop loss and take profit
Entry
Sell limit at 4,294.29, the bottom edge of the 1H supply zone.
The zone is the start of the fall that broke two lows.
The order is placed once the breaks have closed, and left until price returns.
Price went about 31 points past the entry before turning.
Stop loss
4,349.84, above the zone and the sweep high. 55.55 points.
Above about 4,347 the protected high has broken and the short has no reason left.
The buffer is about 3 points. On an index this volatile that is thin.
Add the spread: a sell is closed at the buy price, which is above the chart price.
Take profit
About 4,017, just above the 1H demand zone. About 277 points.
The first opposing zone below the entry.
The low near 4,050 from the second day is taken on the way.
The order sits above the zone edge, so the zone does not have to be entered.
Position size with a 55.55-point stop
Size = money at risk ÷ (stop in points × value of one point per lot). The value of a point and the smallest lot for this index are set by the broker, so read them from the contract specification in your platform first. As an example only: if one lot moves $1 per point, a 55.55-point stop costs $55.55 per lot, and 1% of a $1,000 account ($10) is 10 ÷ 55.55 ≈ 0.18 lots. If the smallest lot allowed risks more than your limit, the trade is too big for the account.

entries.h: What was done well and what to tighten
entries.t:
Review
What was done well and what to tighten
Done well
The break of the lows came after a sweep of a high.
The zone traded is the one that caused the break, and it was fresh.
The entry waited for the lower high in front of the zone to be taken.
The stop was beyond the protected high and was not moved during the rally back.
The target was the first opposing zone, placed just before it.
To tighten
No higher timeframe is shown. Check the 4H direction before using a 1H zone.
No lower-timeframe shift is shown at the entry. Decide whether you trade this as an aggressive entry, and backtest it as its own model.
The stop buffer is about 3 points on an index that moves about 160 a day.
Write down the total risk before adding positions.
Record how far the trade went against you. Here it was about 31 points at entry and 28 points a day later.

entries.h: The steps for the next short like this
entries.t:
Repeatable
The steps for the next short like this
Has a high been swept and then a low broken?Yes, with a candle close below the low. Direction: short.
Where is the protected high?The top of the sweep. Marked.
Where is the supply that caused the break?The last up candle before the fall. Fresh, and in the upper half of the move.
Where is the target?The top of the first demand zone below, at least 1:2 away.
Is there a high in front of the zone?If so, wait for it to be taken.
Confirmation or not?Preferably a lower-timeframe sweep and shift inside the zone. If entering on the touch, say so in the journal.
Orders?Sell limit at the bottom edge. Stop above the protected high plus buffer and spread. Target before the demand.
Size?0.5–1% in total, including any positions added later.
What cancels it?A close above the protected high, or the target being reached before the fill.

entries.h: When this setup should be skipped
entries.t:
Filters
When this setup should be skipped
Do not take it if
The low broke without a high being swept first.
The supply zone has already been touched.
The demand zone is closer than 1:2 from the entry.
A 1H candle has closed above the protected high.
The higher timeframe has just broken upward.
The smallest position your broker allows risks more than your limit.
This trade had all of these
A sweep of a high, then two breaks of structure down.
A fresh supply zone at the start of the fall.
A lower high taken on the way back to the zone.
A stop above the protected high.
A demand zone about 4.9R away.
Keep this in proportion
This is one winning trade on a paper account, on an index whose prices are generated by its provider. It shows the routine being followed well. It does not show that the routine makes money on this index. Test at least fifty setups on Volatility 75 (1s) in replay, as their own set, before trading it with real money.

entries.p: XAU/USD: Two Swept Highs, One Supply Short
entries.h: The retracement sweeps two highs, and that is the warning
entries.t:
Chart: Fifteen-minute chart of gold spot on the FOREX.com feed in replay, panned left. An early MSS line sits near 3,904.5 at the left edge. A red line near 3,906.5 carries an X where a wick sweeps it. Price falls, bounces to a red line near 3,899.8, falls again through a bos line near 3,872.7, sweeps that low with a wick marked X near 3,872.4, then rallies: an MSS line near 3,877.13 is crossed upward and the rally wicks through the 3,899.8 line to about 3,901.3 at 19:00.
Screenshot 1 of 4 — 15m, replay, panned left. The evening opens as a 15m down move, and the retracement that follows sweeps two marked highs before it is over.
Step 1 · Structure
The retracement sweeps two highs, and that is the warning
What the chart shows
MSS near 3,904.5 at the left edge. The 15m shifted down early. The evening begins as a down move, not a range.
The X at about 3,906.5. A wick to about 3,907.5 takes that high: buy-side liquidity collected at the ceiling before the real fall.
The fall, the bounce, the second line at about 3,899.8. Price drops to about 3,878.5 and rallies back to 3,899.8, a lower high under the swept ceiling.
bos at about 3,872.7, then the X at about 3,872.4. The next leg closes below that low, and around 16:00 a wick re-sweeps it. Break, then sweep of the break: the sell-side is clean.
MSS up at 3,877.13. The rally closes above the last lower high. The retracement is on.
The wick through 3,899.8 at 19:00, to about 3,901.3. The second marked high is taken. Two X highs swept on one retracement.
Why it matters
A retracement that sweeps one high is a pullback. A retracement that sweeps two is a pullback that has eaten the liquidity above it, and liquidity eaten above a down move is what makes the next fall travel. Every level that could stop the short on the way down has already been removed on the way up. That is why the supply formed by the next fall deserves an order, and why the sketch in the next screenshot points down.
Rule to carry forward
Count what the retracement sweeps. Two swept highs against the trend are the setup loading; the shift back with the trend is the trigger.

entries.p: XAU/USD: Two Swept Highs, One Supply Short
entries.h: The close below 3,877.13, and a plan drawn in calm
entries.t:
Chart: The same chart panned right at the same moment. From the 3,901.3 high price falls, closes below the MSS line at 3,877.13, wicks to about 3,861.5 into the top of a grey demand box labelled 3,862.87, and recovers to 3,877. A grey supply box spans 3,884.31 to 3,896.86 with a third X line near 3,893.3 at its left edge, and a sketched plan rises into the box then arrows down to about 3,865.5. A second grey demand box spans 3,852.48 to 3,862.87 at the bottom.
Screenshot 2 of 4 — the same moment, panned right. The shift down has printed, the supply is drawn, and the whole plan exists on the chart before price is anywhere near it.
Step 2 · The shift and the plan
The close below 3,877.13, and a plan drawn in calm
What the chart shows
The fall from 3,901.3. One leg, no drama, straight back through the retracement.
The close below the MSS at 3,877.13. This is the trigger: the 15m has shifted down again, with the trend, after both highs were swept. Everything before this was context.
The wick to about 3,861.5. It tags the top of the lower demand, 3,862.87, and bounces. The first fall always probes what is below; that probe is not the trade.
The grey box, 3,884.31 to 3,896.86. The supply left by the fall that just shifted structure. Drawn now, while price sits at 3,877, ten points away.
The third X at about 3,893.3. The last internal high inside that supply: the liquidity sitting above the future entry.
The sketch. A zigzag up into the box, then one long arrow down to about 3,865.5. The entire trade in two strokes: retest, then fall into the demand.
The two grey boxes below. A thin one near 3,862.5–3,866.5 and the labelled demand 3,852.48–3,862.87: the floor the arrow points at.
Why it matters
Compare this with most losses: the zone, the stop level and the target are all on the chart while price is ten points away and nothing is urgent. When price finally arrives there is nothing left to decide. The sketch also names the end of the trade before it starts, which is the habit that keeps a winner from being given back.
Rule to carry forward
Draw the trade at the shift, not at the tag. If the zone, the invalidation and the target cannot be drawn in calm, they will not survive contact.

entries.p: XAU/USD: Two Swept Highs, One Supply Short
entries.h: Price arrives, and the plan becomes three numbers
entries.t:
Chart: The same chart minutes later. Price has rallied from about 3,872 to about 3,885, into the bottom of the supply, which is now drawn in red with both edges labelled 3,896.86 and 3,884.31. A blue box spans 3,884.31 down to 3,860.50 under the supply, and the sketched arrow still points down to about 3,865.5 into the grey demand labelled 3,862.87 and 3,852.48. Price sits at 3,885.12.
Screenshot 3 of 4 — price arrives. The supply turns red, the corridor under it is drawn, and every number the order needs is already labelled on the axis.
Step 3 · Delivery
Price arrives, and the plan becomes three numbers
What the chart shows
The rally from the 3,872 tag to about 3,885. Straight into the bottom edge of the supply. No sweep of the X at 3,893.3 on the way: price enters the zone from underneath without taking the internal high.
The supply turns red, edges labelled 3,896.86 and 3,884.31. The zone is live. The labels are the order: sell at the near edge, which for a short is the bottom one.
The blue box, 3,884.31 down to 3,860.50. The corridor under the supply: the internal range and imbalance the fall has to travel through. It is drawn before the fall, not after it.
The targets on the axis. 3,862.87 in white and 3,860.50 in blue at the corridor floor, the demand 3,852.48–3,862.87 below that, and the sketch arrow ending near 3,865.5.
Why it matters
A sell limit at 3,884.31 fills on this rally as price crosses the edge on its way up. That is the whole execution: no market order, no chasing the tag, no decision at the candle. The corridor matters too, because it tells you what “going well” looks like mid-trade: price inside the blue box, making lower highs along it, is a trade to hold; a close back above 3,884.31 is not.
Rule to carry forward
For a short, the near edge of supply is its bottom. Put the limit there and let the rally deliver it; a close back over that edge before the fall is the setup asking to be re-checked.

entries.p: XAU/USD: Two Swept Highs, One Supply Short
entries.h: Two points in, then the whole corridor
entries.t:
Chart: The same chart at the end of the move, Monday 16 November 07:15. Price tagged about two points into the red supply near 3,886.5, then fell through the blue corridor along a dashed internal trendline, broke 3,860.50 and the demand top 3,862.87 with a displacement candle, wicked to about 3,847.5 below the demand bottom, and bounced to about 3,855. The X line at 3,893.3 was never touched. Price sits at 3,854.975.
Screenshot 4 of 4 — the run. Two points into the zone, down the corridor, through both corridor floor and demand top, wick to 3,847.5, bounce at 3,855.
Step 4 · Outcome
Two points in, then the whole corridor
What the chart shows
The tag at about 3,886.5. Two points into a twelve-point zone. The limit at 3,884.31 filled on the way up; the top at 3,896.86 was never tested, and neither was the X at 3,893.3.
The fall along the dashed line. Lower highs inside the blue corridor, exactly the “going well” picture from the last section.
The displacement candle through 3,860.50 and 3,862.87. Corridor floor and demand top go in one candle. Both labelled targets are hit here.
The wick to about 3,847.5 and the bounce to 3,855. Below the demand bottom, 3,852.48, on a wick: the demand did its job as a floor on the first test, and the move is over.
Why it matters
Three lessons. One: a shallow tag is enough; the zone does not owe you a test of its far edge, which is why the stop lives beyond the whole zone and not beyond the tag. Two: the corridor gives a hold rule for free, and this trade never broke it until the targets were already paid. Three: the X at 3,893.3 stayed above the entry the entire trade and was never taken. On this site’s inducement page that liquidity above a short is usually taken first; here it was not. Log it as the exception it is, not as permission to ignore it next time.
Rule to carry forward
When the target zone is hit on displacement, take it. The wick beyond it, to 3,847.5, was never the target; demanding it is how a paid trade becomes a given-back one.

entries.p: XAU/USD: Two Swept Highs, One Supply Short
entries.h: The whole evening in ten lines
entries.t:
Everything as one
The whole evening in ten lines
The 15m shifts down early (MSS near 3,904.5); the evening is a down move.
The ceiling high at 3,906.5 is swept by a wick before the real fall.
The fall breaks the low at 3,872.7 (bos) and then re-sweeps it (X at 3,872.4).
The retracement rallies: MSS up at 3,877.13.
It sweeps the second marked high, 3,899.8, at 19:00 (wick 3,901.3).
It then closes back below 3,877.13: the shift down, with both highs already eaten.
The supply 3,884.31–3,896.86 is drawn at the shift, with the X at 3,893.3 inside it and the sketch: retest, then fall to the demand.
Price rallies through the near edge and fills the sell limit at 3,884.31, tagging 3,886.5.
The fall runs down the blue corridor along its dashed internal line.
Displacement breaks 3,860.50 and 3,862.87; the wick prints 3,847.5; the bounce ends it at 3,855.
Read against the full sequence: sweep, shift, zone, target, in that order, with the zone and the target drawn at the shift. Read against your 5m gold long, it is the mirror image: there the sweeps were of lows and the zone was demand; here the sweeps are of highs and the zone is supply. Same routine, other side of the chart.
What is still missing
As with the 5m case, no higher timeframe appears in any of the four screenshots. A 15m supply inside 4H demand is a scalp with a floor one candle away; the same 15m supply inside 4H supply is the best short on the board. One 4H or 1H screenshot before the session is the difference, and it costs nothing to capture.

entries.p: XAU/USD: Two Swept Highs, One Supply Short
entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit
entries.t:
The order
Entry, stop loss and take profit
| Part | Level | Why there
| Entry | Sell limit 3,884.31 | The near edge of the supply, which for a short is its bottom. The rally from 3,872 crosses it and fills the limit; the tag to 3,886.5 goes two points in.
| Stop | 3,897.40 | Above the zone top, 3,896.86, plus a small buffer. A close over the whole supply is the idea being wrong. Risk about 13.1 of price.
| Target 1 | 3,863.40 | A touch above the demand top, 3,862.87, and just past the corridor floor. Reward about 20.9, near 1:1.6.
| Target 2 (the rule target) | 3,853.00 | Inside the demand, above its bottom at 3,852.48. Reward about 31.3, near 1:2.4. The wick to 3,847.5 was extra, not owed.
| Size | Fixed risk | Work out what 13.1 of price costs per lot on your feed first, then size so that amount equals 0.5–1% of the account.
Same warning as the 5m case: the first target is too close
1:1.6 to the demand top is under this site’s 1:2 floor. The trade only earns its place because the demand zone sits behind that first line and pays 1:2.4. Two gold cases in a row with a sub-1:2 first target is now a pattern in the log, not an accident: name the zone, not the line in front of it, when you size the idea.
The tighter stop, and why it stays a temptation
A stop above the internal X at 3,893.3 risks about 9.7 instead of 13.1 and lifts the reward-to-risk to about 1:2.2 and 1:3.2. It also dies the first time that X does what Xs do and gets swept. The rule does not change: the stop sits beyond the structure that invalidates the idea, which here is the whole supply zone.

entries.p: XAU/USD: Two Swept Highs, One Supply Short
entries.h: What worked, and what to fix
entries.t:
Review
What worked, and what to fix
Done well
Both swept highs marked with an X before the shift down, so the setup could be counted, not felt.
The supply drawn at the shift, ten points away from price, with both edges labelled to the cent.
The plan sketched in two strokes: retest, then fall to a named floor.
The corridor drawn before the fall, giving a free hold rule mid-trade.
Targets on the axis before the entry, and the move closed when they were paid.
To fix or answer
No position line or filled ticket in any of the four screenshots. If the short was never placed, this session belongs in the log as a missed execution, and the miss has a cause worth naming.
The first target is under 1:2 again. Size the idea to the zone behind the line.
The X at 3,893.3 was left above the entry and never taken. It worked; that is the exception, and the inducement page explains why it usually will not.
Still no higher-timeframe screenshot. Third request: capture the 1H or 4H before the session.

entries.p: XAU/USD: Two Swept Highs, One Supply Short
entries.h: Run this the same way every session
entries.t:
Repeatable steps
Run this the same way every session
Name the trend from the last shift, and mark the ceiling and floor it left.Here: MSS down near 3,904.5, ceiling 3,906.5, floor 3,872.7.
Let the retracement run and count what it sweeps.One swept high is a pullback; two is a loaded setup. Do not trade the retracement itself.
Wait for the close back through the shift level, with the trend.The close below 3,877.13. Before it, the supply does not exist yet.
Draw the zone the shift left, both edges, while price is away from it.3,884.31 to 3,896.86, drawn at 3,877.
Mark the internal liquidity inside the zone and the floor below it.The X at 3,893.3 above the entry; the demand 3,852.48–3,862.87 as the target.
Place the three numbers as one order.Limit at the near edge, stop beyond the whole zone plus buffer, target inside the opposing zone. Require 1:2 to that target or skip.
Hold while price respects the corridor; re-check on a close back over the near edge.Lower highs inside the fall range are the trade working.
Take the target when it is hit on displacement, and close the plan with it.The wick beyond is not yours. The next idea starts from the new structure.

Two screenshots from your replay of gold on the FOREX.com feed, Friday 13 November. The 5m falls and breaks a low, sweeps it, and shifts up. The pullback builds a double bottom, that gets swept too, and the 5m shifts a second time. The demand left by the second shift is marked to the cent, price tags into its top edge, and the rally runs through the marked $$$ high and through the supply above it.

These are your two screenshots in TradingView replay mode, in order, with your own marks: bos, MSS, X for a swept low, $$$ for resting liquidity, a red demand box with both edges labelled (3,878.52 and 3,869.37), a purple box up to 3,892.14, grey boxes for the supply above and the older demands below, and a sketched plan at the right edge.
