entries.h: The fall, the two sweeps and the second shift
entries.t:
Chart: Five-minute chart of gold spot on the FOREX.com feed in replay. A fall from about 3,899 breaks a low near 3,872.9, marked bos, with the final low marked X near 3,872.3. A first MSS is marked above about 3,882. The rally to about 3,890.5 leaves a red $$$ line. The pullback makes a double bottom near 3,872.5 underlined in red with an X, a wick sweeps it to about 3,870.9, and a second MSS is marked above about 3,878.4. A red demand box spans 3,869.37 to 3,878.52, two grey demand boxes sit below and left of it, a purple box spans 3,878.52 to 3,892.14, and a grey supply box sits above about 3,892.6 with a small sketched up-then-down plan at the right. Price stands at 3,883.44.
Screenshot 1 — 5m, replay, Fri 13 Nov. Both sweeps and both shifts are marked, and the demand, the targets and the supply above are drawn before price returns to the zone.
Step 1 · Structure and zones
The fall, the two sweeps and the second shift
What the chart shows
bos at about 3,872.9, X under it. The falling leg from 3,899 closes below that low, and the X candle, about 3,872.3, is the final low of the break.
First MSS above about 3,882.4. The bounce closes over the last lower high. The fall is over for now.
The rally to about 3,890.5 and the $$$ line. The high that rally leaves behind is resting buy-side liquidity, labelled before price ever comes back to it.
The double bottom near 3,872.5, underlined in red, X on the first low. Two near-equal lows: sell-side liquidity sitting under the pullback.
The wick to about 3,870.9. That liquidity is taken. A stop hunt under the pullback, one candle, and it is done.
Second MSS above about 3,878.4. The rally out of the sweep closes over the last lower high. This is the shift the entry waits for.
The red box, 3,869.37 to 3,878.52. The base of that second shift: the 5m demand, both edges labelled to the cent. The two grey boxes below and left of it are the older bases under the double bottom, the floor the red zone stands on.
The purple box, 3,878.52 to 3,892.14. The range the rally has to travel, with its top labelled just above the $$$ line: the first objective.
The grey box above about 3,892.6 and the sketch at the right. Higher supply, and the plan in one line: up into it taking the $$$, then rejection.
Why it matters
Everything a limit order needs is on the chart while price is still away from the zone: the direction (second MSS up), the level that proves the idea wrong (under the red box), the place to buy (the top edge of the red box), the first target (the $$$ high and the purple top) and the place the idea ends (the supply above). Nothing here is decided in a hurry at the edge.
Rule to carry forward
Draw the zone, the stop level and the target while price is still away from the zone. A plan drawn in a hurry at the edge is a chase, not a plan.

entries.h: The zone holds once and the rally runs through everything
entries.t:
Chart: The same chart later in the replay. Price has tagged into the top of the red demand with a wick near 3,876, rallied, pulled back to about 3,881.5 above the zone top, then pushed with large blue candles through the $$$ line near 3,891.3, through the purple top at 3,892.14 and through the grey supply box, to 3,900.48 at the top of the chart. A crosshair sits at 15:25 on the earlier session.
Screenshot 2 — the same session, later. The tag into the zone, the pullback that holds above it, and the run through every marked target.
Step 2 · Delivery and outcome
The zone holds once and the rally runs through everything
What the chart shows
The tag. A wick to about 3,875.5, a third of the way into the red zone. A buy limit at the top edge, 3,878.52, fills on the way in.
The pullback to about 3,881.5. It holds above the zone top. That is the first evidence the zone is doing its job, and the last chance to enter at market if the limit missed.
Displacement. Large blue candles through the $$$ line near 3,891.3 and through the purple top at 3,892.14. The liquidity labelled in screenshot 1 is taken exactly as labelled.
The close above the grey supply, price at 3,900.48. The sketched rejection never prints. The supply above is broken on its first test, in one session.
Why it matters
Three separate lessons in one run. A zone only has to hold once: one tag is the whole test. Liquidity labelled before the rally gets taken: the $$$ line did its job as a target. And a plan that ends at a supply must be remade the moment that supply closes beyond: the sketch said “up then down”, the chart said “up and closed above”, and the second half of the sketch died there. The long keeps its profit; the short from that supply never gets to exist.
Rule to carry forward
When price closes through the zone your target sat in front of, the trade is done and the next idea starts fresh. Never short the break of your own target.

entries.h: The whole session in ten lines
entries.t:
Everything as one
The whole session in ten lines
The fall from 3,899 breaks the low at 3,872.9 (bos), final low 3,872.3 (X).
First MSS above 3,882.4: the fall is over.
The rally to 3,890.5 leaves the $$$ high behind it.
The pullback builds a double bottom near 3,872.5, underlined in red.
A wick sweeps it to 3,870.9: the sell-side liquidity is taken.
Second MSS above 3,878.4: the shift the entry waits for.
The red 5m demand is drawn, 3,869.37 to 3,878.52, with the $$$ high, the purple top at 3,892.14 and the supply above all labelled, plus the sketched plan.
Price tags the top edge: the entry, a wick a third into the zone.
The pullback holds above the zone top at 3,881.5.
The rally takes the $$$ high and 3,892.14, closes through the supply, and prints 3,900.48.
That is this site’s model in order — sweep, shift, zone, target — on one 5m chart in one session, with one extra discipline worth copying: the target was named before the entry, not after the rally started.
What is different from the other cases
Everything here is one timeframe. No 1H or 4H is shown, so nothing on these two screenshots says whether the long was with or against the bigger flow. In replay that is acceptable practice; on a live account the higher timeframes decide whether a 5m demand is the best trade on the board or a counter-trend scalp. See Top-down analysis.

entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit
entries.t:
The order
Entry, stop loss and take profit
| Part | Level | Why there
| Entry | Buy limit 3,878.52 | The near (top) edge of the red 5m demand. The tag wick to 3,875.5 fills it.
| Stop | 3,868.90 | Below the zone bottom, 3,869.37, with a small buffer. A close under the zone is the idea being wrong, so the stop lives under it. Risk about 9.6 of price.
| Target 1 | 3,890.90 | A few cents before the $$$ high at 3,891.3. Reward about 12.4, near 1:1.3.
| Target 2 (the rule target) | About 3,899 | The far side of the grey supply. Reward about 20.5, near 1:2.1. This is the target that makes the trade worth taking.
| Size | Fixed risk | Work out what 9.6 of price costs per lot on your feed first, then size so that amount equals 0.5–1% of the account.
The first target is too close
1:1.3 to the $$$ high is under this site’s 1:2 floor, and the purple top at 3,892.14 is only 1:1.4. Naming that liquidity before the rally is excellent work; sizing the trade to it while a supply zone sits behind it is the one mistake on these charts. Either the target is the far side of the supply, near 1:2.1, or the setup is a skip. Measure both distances before the order, not after the tag.
The tighter stop, and why it is not the rule
A stop under the sweep wick, near 3,870.40, risks about 8.1 instead of 9.6 and lifts the reward-to-risk on both targets. It also dies the moment the double bottom is swept a second time, which is a normal thing for a double bottom to do. The rule stays: the stop goes beyond the structure that invalidates the idea, which here is the zone bottom.

entries.h: What worked, and what to fix
entries.t:
Review
What worked, and what to fix
Done well
Both sweeps marked with an X, and the double bottom underlined, before the sweep happened.
The demand drawn only after the second MSS, not on the first bounce.
Zone edges labelled to the cent, so the limit and the stop are numbers, not feelings.
The $$$ target labelled before the rally, then taken exactly there.
A sketched end to the plan: rejection at the supply above.
To fix or answer
No order ticket or position line in either screenshot. If the long was never placed, the cost is the whole move, and the pullback at 3,881.5 was the second chance at market.
The reward-to-risk as marked, to the first target, is under 1:2. The supply behind it is the real target.
The sketched rejection failed: price closed above the supply. The “then down” half of the plan had to be deleted on that close.
The purple box is my guess (the range to the first objective). Tell me what you meant by it and I will correct the page.
The question to ask this chart
Where was the 1H? A 5m demand inside 1H supply is a counter-trend scalp with a ceiling; the same 5m demand inside 1H demand is the best trade on the board. One extra screenshot of the 1H before the session answers it, and it costs nothing.

entries.h: Run this the same way every session
entries.t:
Repeatable steps
Run this the same way every session
Let the fall break its low, and mark that low and the sweep of it.The bos line and the X under the final low. Before this there is nothing to trade.
Wait for the first MSS.The bounce that closes over the last lower high. Do not buy the bounce before it prints.
Mark the high the first rally leaves.That $$$ line is a target for the long, never a place to sell from.
Wait for the pullback liquidity to be swept.Double bottoms, equal lows, trendline lows: whatever rests under the pullback gets taken first.
On the sweep, wait for the second MSS, then draw the demand at its base.Exact edges. The base of the displacement, not the middle of the pullback.
Place the three numbers as one order.Limit at the near edge, stop below the zone plus buffer, target at the labelled liquidity and then the zone behind it. Require 1:2 to that zone target or skip.
Let the tag fill, or miss it.No chasing. The pullback that holds above the zone top is the last market entry.
When the target zone closes through, close the plan with it.Read the chart again from the new structure. The old sketch is dead paper.

entries.h: Introduction
entries.t:
Case study · XAU/USD
Textbook Institutional Flow
A short on gold taken with the 4H trend. The 4H swept a high and shifted bearish. Price then pulled back, ran the highs that traders were hiding stops above, and shifted down on the 15m. The entry was the return to the 15-minute order block, with the demand zone below as the target.
Short
4H → 1H → 15m
Target: 15m demand
TP hit · ≈ 1:3.8
HTF bias4H sweep of the high, then bearish MSS
Location1H pullback, upper half of the drop
Liquidity taken1H internal high, then two more highs
Confirmation15m MSS with displacement
EntryBottom edge of the 15m order block
Stop lossJust above the order block
Take profitTop edge of the demand zone
OutcomeTarget reached, ≈ 3.8R
1 · 4H sweep and shift
2 · 1H pullback
3 · 15m shift
4 · Entry
5 · Result
Everything as one
Entry, SL & TP
Repeatable steps
When to skip
How to read this page
On these charts X marks a liquidity sweep: a wick runs a high and price turns back. The slides have no price axis, so levels are described by structure. The reward-to-risk figure is measured from the position boxes: the blue box is a little under four times the height of the grey one. Times are as printed on the charts.

entries.h: 4H: sweep the high, shift down
entries.t:
Chart: 4-hour gold chart. A wick takes out an earlier high (X), price sells off and closes below the previous swing low (MSS), then bounces.
Slide 1 — 4H chart. “Price sweeps the high, then shifts structure down.”
Step 1 · Bias
4H: sweep the high, shift down
This slide sets the direction for everything that follows.
What happened
An old high was left standing. The first peak on the left is the reference high. Buy stops from sellers and breakout orders from buyers collect above it.
Price came back and swept it (X). Days later a candle pushed above that high and could not hold there. The following candles closed back underneath. The buy-side liquidity was taken and there was no continuation.
Structure shifted bearish (MSS). The sell-off that followed closed below the swing low between the two peaks. The 4H is no longer making higher lows.
A pullback began. The last few candles on the slide are a bounce off the low. That bounce is what the lower timeframes zoom into.
Why this matters
Sweep, then shift. A break of structure that comes straight after a liquidity grab is more trustworthy than one that comes from nowhere. The high was used to fill sell orders.
The bounce is now a selling opportunity. After a bearish 4H MSS, rallies are pullbacks until proven otherwise. The job is to find where the pullback ends.
The trade is with the higher timeframe. Everything below is about timing a short in the direction the 4H has already chosen.
Rule to carry forward
Take shorts only after the 4H has swept a high and closed below the last swing low. Then wait for the pullback. Do not sell the breakdown candle itself: it is the most expensive place to enter.

entries.h: 1H: the pullback runs an internal high
entries.t:
Chart: 1-hour gold chart. After a steep drop, price climbs back, takes out an internal high from inside the drop (X), takes one more small high (X), then prints a bearish candle.
Slide 2 — 1H chart. “Zoom in. Price pullback, sweep internal high and start moving down.”
Step 2 · Location and liquidity
1H: the pullback runs an internal high
The 1H shows how far the bounce travels and what it takes on the way.
What happened
The drop left an internal high. Partway down the sell-off, one candle made a small high before price continued lower. The long X line starts from it. Traders who sold the drop tend to put stops above a high like this.
Price climbed back in a slow grind. Small overlapping candles for many hours. Compare that with the speed of the drop: the pullback is corrective, the drop was impulsive.
First sweep (long X). A large bullish candle finally pushed through the internal high. By then price had recovered well over half of the drop, so it was in premium.
Second sweep (short X). Price made one more marginal high above the candle that did the first sweep, with wicks only.
A bearish candle followed. The last candle on the slide is the first decisive move down since the pullback began.
Why this is the location
There is no supply box drawn on this slide. The point of interest is the liquidity itself. The pullback has reached the upper half of the bearish leg and has taken the stops that were resting inside it. Sellers now have both a good price and the orders they need to fill against.
Rule to carry forward
In a bearish pullback, mark the internal highs left inside the drop. The short setup begins when price is above the 50% level of the leg and one of those highs has been swept. Before that, the pullback is still shopping for liquidity.
Common mistake
Selling the first touch of the internal high. Price swept it and then went on to take a second high on the 1H and a third on the 15m. The sweep says “watch”. Only a structure shift says “sell”.

entries.h: 15m: three breaks up, a sweep, then the shift
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute gold chart. Three breaks of structure upward, a sweep of the higher-timeframe high (X), a second sweep (X), then a close below the last higher low (MSS).
Slide 3 — 15m chart. “Structure breaks up a few times. Then price sweeps the high and shifts down.”
Step 3 · Confirmation
15m: three breaks up, a sweep, then the shift
What happened
The 15m was bullish on the way up. Three BoS labels mark three higher highs. On this timeframe alone, it looks like an uptrend worth buying.
The 1H internal high was taken (long X). The long horizontal line is the same high from slide 2. The third leg up runs straight through it.
A higher low formed, then one more high (short X). Price dipped, then pushed up again and took the high it had just made. This is the second sweep.
MSS. Price then closed below the higher low that sat between the two sweeps. For the first time in the whole rally, a 15m low failed.
Why this matters
Each break of structure on the way up recruits buyers and gives them a place to put stops. By the third one, the lows underneath are loaded with sell stops and late buyers are entering at the highs, exactly where the 4H wants to sell. The MSS is the first evidence that the 15m has stopped disagreeing with the 4H.
Rule to carry forward
Let the lower timeframe trend against you into the higher-timeframe liquidity. The signal is the sequence: the HTF high is swept, then a candle closes below the most recent 15m higher low. Use the low that produced the final high, not a minor one inside the last leg.

entries.h: Entry: order block under a protected high
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute gold chart with the short planned. An order block sits above an imbalance and below the protected high; the target is the top of the demand zone, with equal lows on the way.
Slide 4 — 15m chart with the order planned. “Price returns to the order block and the protected high stays intact.”
Step 4 · Refinement and order placement
Entry: order block under a protected high
This slide is frozen shortly after the shift. Everything needed to place the order is on it.
What is marked
A third X and the protected high. Just before the drop, one wick took out a small high. That wick is the last high made before the displacement, so it becomes the protected high. If price trades above it, the bearish shift has failed.
OB. The last bullish candles before the displacement candle. This is where the selling that broke structure began.
IMB. The displacement candle left an imbalance directly under the order block. A pullback that fills it arrives at the bottom of the OB.
MSS. The broken higher low, a little below the OB.
EQL. Equal lows left during the rally. Two lows at the same price mean a thick layer of sell stops underneath. It sits between entry and target and helps pull price down.
Demand. The zone at the base of the 15m rally. It is the first place buyers are likely to respond, so the target is its top edge.
Why the entry is here
The order block is the origin of the move that broke structure, it sits in premium on every timeframe shown, and the imbalance beneath it gives price a reason to come back. Entry is a sell limit at the bottom edge of the OB, the first price a pullback reaches after filling the imbalance.
The stop on the chart sits just above the top of the order block, a little under the protected high. That keeps the risk small. Measured against it, the distance down to demand is about 3.8 times the risk.
Rule to carry forward
After a bearish MSS, mark the last bullish candle before the displacement and the high above it. Sell the bottom edge of that order block only while the protected high is intact and only if an imbalance separates the OB from current price.

entries.h: Result
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute gold chart after the trade. Price ranges below the order block, spikes into its bottom edge, then sells off through the equal lows to the top of the demand zone.
Slide 5 — the same chart after the trade played out.
Step 5 · Management and outcome
Result
What happened
Price went sideways first. For roughly two hours after the shift it ranged underneath the order block without reaching it.
One push filled the order. Around 06:00 on the chart a candle ran up through the imbalance and touched the bottom of the OB. The next candle was strongly bearish.
The protected high was never tested. Price did not travel past the lower part of the order block.
Sell-off through the equal lows. Price fell in a steady staircase, cleared the EQL, and kept going.
Target reached. The bottom of the blue box is the top edge of demand. Price hit it and wicked slightly inside.
What to take from it
The fill was shallow again. As in the USD/JPY trade, price only just reached the near edge of the order block. A sell limit in the middle of the OB would have been left behind.
The range before the fill was a test of patience. Nothing in those two hours changed the plan: the protected high was intact and the order was resting.
Equal lows were fuel, not the exit. The target was the demand zone beyond them. The EQL is a sensible place for a partial if you take one.
Rule to carry forward
While waiting for a fill, the only question is whether the protected high has been broken. If it has, cancel. If it has not, leave the order alone.

entries.h: The whole trade in a single picture
entries.t:
Everything as one
The whole trade in a single picture
A schematic of the 15m sequence, not a copy of the chart. The 4H has already swept its high and shifted bearish before this picture starts.
1 · SWEEP THE HTF HIGH
The 15m rallies out of demand with three breaks of structure and runs the 1H internal high. Stops above the pullback are taken in premium.
2 · SWEEP AGAIN
A higher low forms, then price takes the high it just made. A last small sweep sets the protected high.
3 · SHIFT
A displacement candle closes below the higher low. It leaves an imbalance under the order block.
4 · ENTRY
After a two-hour range, price fills the imbalance and touches the bottom of the order block, where the sell limit is resting.
5 · TARGET
Price sells off through the equal lows to the top of the demand zone that started the rally. About 3.8R.
THE LOGIC IN ONE SENTENCE
Sell the first pullback after the 15m flips bearish at swept HTF highs, risk the order block, and take profit at the first demand below.

entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit
entries.t:
Order placement
Entry, stop loss and take profit
Entry
Sell limit at the bottom edge of the 15m order block.
Place it when the MSS candle closes.
The bottom edge is where the imbalance ends, so it is the first price a pullback reaches.
Price only touched that edge here. A deeper order would not have filled.
Sells fill on the bid, which is the charted price. No spread adjustment is needed on the entry.
Stop loss
Just above the top of the order block, plus spread.
This is where the grey box ends on the chart: above the OB, slightly below the protected high.
Reason: if price trades through the whole order block, the sellers there have been absorbed.
A short is closed by a buy stop, which triggers on the ask. Gold spreads can be wide, so add the spread to the stop.
More conservative: above the protected high. That is the true structural invalidation. On this chart it would have cut the trade to roughly 1:3.
Take profit
Top edge of the demand zone. About 3.8R.
It is the first opposing zone: the base of the rally that carried price up into the highs.
The equal lows sit above it, so price has liquidity to reach for on the way down.
The target is the near edge. Buyers may respond anywhere inside the zone.
A short's take profit fills on the ask. Set it a little above the zone edge, by the spread plus a small margin.
Managing the position
The post shows a single entry and a single exit. The points below are my suggested handling, not something marked on the slides.
Leave the stop alone until price closes below the post-MSS low and prints a new 15m lower high. Then it can trail to just above that lower high.
Optional partial at the equal lows. Decide before entry.
Cancel the limit if the protected high breaks, or if price covers about half the distance to demand without filling you.
Position size on gold
Fix the money at risk first, then let the stop distance decide the lot size.
Lots = money at risk ÷ (stop in dollars × 100)
One standard lot of XAU/USD is normally 100 ounces, so a $1 move in gold is $100 per lot. Check your broker's contract size, because some differ.
Example: $10,000 account, 1% risk = $100. A stop of $5.00 gives 100 ÷ (5 × 100) = 0.20 lots. At 1:3.8 the target pays about $380.

entries.h: Step-by-step for the next trade
entries.t:
Repeatable strategy
Step-by-step for the next trade
Written for shorts, as in this trade. For longs, mirror it: lows for highs, discount for premium, supply for demand. A “no” at any step ends the process.
Has the 4H swept a high and closed below the last swing low?Both are needed. This gives the bearish bias. Mark the leg from the swept high to the new low and its 50% level.
On the 1H, mark the internal highs inside the drop.These are the liquidity the pullback is likely to reach for. Set an alert at the nearest one above the 50% level.
Has the pullback swept an internal high in premium?It should arrive as a corrective grind, slower than the drop. No sweep, no setup.
Drop to the 15m and mark the most recent higher low.The rally will show several breaks of structure up. Keep moving the line to the low that produced the latest high.
Did a candle close below that higher low with displacement?This is the MSS. It should leave an imbalance. A wick below the low does not count.
Mark the order block and the protected high.The OB is the last bullish candle before the displacement. The protected high is the highest point just before the drop. The OB must be untouched since the shift.
Does it pay at least 1:2 to the first demand below?Measure entry at the OB's bottom edge, stop above the OB (or above the protected high), target at the top edge of demand.
Place the orders.Sell limit, stop and target together. Size for a fixed 0.5–1% of the account. Add the spread to the stop.
Manage by structure, then record it.Cancel if the protected high breaks before the fill. Once in, hold to target, stop, or a new lower high you can trail above. Screenshot the 4H, 1H and 15m.

entries.h: When this setup should be skipped
entries.t:
Filters
When this setup should be skipped
Do not take it if
The 4H has not shifted. A sweep of a high without a close below the swing low is not a bias.
The pullback is still in the lower half of the 4H drop.
The 1H pullback closes above the high the 4H swept. The bearish idea is over.
The 15m “shift” breaks only a minor low, or leaves no imbalance.
The protected high is taken before the order fills.
Demand is so close that the trade pays less than 1:2.
High-impact USD news is due before the pullback is likely to fill. Gold spreads widen sharply around it.
This trade had all of these
4H sweep of a high followed by a bearish MSS.
A corrective 1H pullback into the upper half of the drop.
The 1H internal high swept, then two more highs.
15m MSS on a displacement candle with an imbalance.
An untouched order block under an intact protected high.
Equal lows and an unmitigated demand zone below, about 3.8R away.
Compared with the USD/JPY trade
| | USD/JPY long | XAU/USD short
| HTF bias | 4H sweep of a low, bullish MSS | 4H sweep of a high, bearish MSS
| Where the pullback ended | In a drawn 4H demand zone | At swept 1H internal highs, no zone drawn
| Confirmation | 30m MSS | 15m MSS
| Entry | Near edge of 15m OB, after an imbalance | Near edge of 15m OB, after an imbalance
| Stop on the chart | Beyond the sweep low that launched the MSS | Beyond the order block, inside the protected high
| Target | Near edge of first opposing supply | Near edge of first opposing demand
| Fill | Wick into the OB edge | Touch of the OB edge
Same skeleton, mirrored. The two differences worth noting are the location (zone versus liquidity) and how tight the stop was drawn.
Keep this in proportion
The tight stop above the order block is what produces 1:3.8, and it is also the easiest part to get wrong. Gold often wicks through an order block toward the protected high before turning. Test both stop placements in your own backtest and compare the results across at least 50 trades before choosing one.

Case study · XAU/USD · TrendForge.FX post
Sweep, MSS, FVG and OB
Four slides from a posted breakdown of gold. The 4H is bearish with liquidity taken above. On the 15m the swing high is swept under a protected high, structure shifts down, and the shift leaves an FVG and a bearish order block for mitigation. Price taps the block about halfway and delivers lower, breaking the session lows. The post’s own line is the lesson: the key is knowing how these concepts work together, not just identifying them on a chart.

How to read this page
These are four of the five slides of the post, in the order the post tells the story: 4H first, then the 15m setup, then the reaction, then the cover board with every mark at once. The slides are stylised and carry no price axis, so this page quotes no prices and no reward-to-risk; the levels are named instead — protected high, OB, FVG, SSL — and the order rules are given in those names. entries.p: XAU/USD: Sweep, MSS, FVG and OB
entries.h: The 4H says which side of the 15m to trade
entries.t:
Chart: Stylised 4H candlestick chart of gold with the price axis stripped. Two large bearish candles fall, a rally follows with a shift mark at its high, then a lower high with a second shift mark, then further falling candles. A dashed rising line labelled with dollar signs connects the low under the fall to the low under the pullback. Slide caption: 4H chart, clear bearish structure, liquidity was taken above.
Slide 2 of the post — the 4H. Two shifts down and a lower high: the structure is bearish, and the high above was already taken.
Step 1 · Higher timeframe
The 4H says which side of the 15m to trade
What the slide shows
Two large bearish candles. The 4H falls hard enough that nothing on the lower timeframes can argue with it.
The first Sh at the rally high. The bounce that follows the fall shifts structure down on its way: the rally never becomes a reversal.
The second Sh at a lower high. A second, lower shift. Bearish structure in two strokes: lower high, then continuation.
“Liquidity was taken above.” The high over the first shift was swept before or as the structure turned. The buy-side above is clean, so nothing rests above to pull price up.
The dashed $$$ line under the lows. Sell-side liquidity resting below on the 4H: the magnet the whole idea points at, two timeframes down.
Why it matters
Nothing is traded on this slide. Its only job is to answer one question: if the 15m offers a short and a long in the same session, which one is taken? With the 4H bearish, its highs swept and its sell-side untouched below, the answer is the short — and every 15m long in that session is a counter-trend scalp against this picture. That is the first line of the post’s caption made concrete: structure on the higher timeframe is what turns a pattern into a plan.
Rule to carry forward
Before any lower-timeframe setup is judged, name the higher-timeframe direction and the liquidity it leaves untouched. The setup trades in that direction or not at all.

entries.p: XAU/USD: Sweep, MSS, FVG and OB
entries.h: Sweep, shift, and a zone worth waiting for
entries.t:
Chart: Stylised 15m candlestick chart of gold with the price axis stripped. A swing high is swept, marked X, under a dashed protected-high line; the rally that sweeps it leaves a pink order block labelled OB with a shift mark at its left edge; an arrow labels an FVG just below the block and a dashed dollar line sits beside it; an MSS label marks the close below the last higher low; a dashed rising trendline of lows runs along the bottom. Slide caption: 15m chart, swing high swept + MSS, leaving an FVG and bearish order block for mitigation.
Slide 3 of the post — the 15m. The sweep, the shift, and the two things the shift leaves behind: an FVG and an order block.
Step 2 · Lower timeframe
Sweep, shift, and a zone worth waiting for
What the slide shows
The X at the swing high. The 15m rallies into the 4H’s ceiling and takes the swing high — buy-side liquidity collected, exactly where the higher timeframe said it would be.
The dashed protected high above it. The high of the sweeping candle. Nothing may close above it while the short idea lives; it is where the stop goes.
MSS down. The fall out of the sweep closes below the last higher low. With the 4H bearish, this shift is with the trend, not against it.
The OB, with Sh at its left edge. The last up candles before the displacement down: the bearish order block, drawn at the shift and left for mitigation.
The FVG at the block’s near edge. The imbalance the displacement left below the OB. Entry at the block’s edge and entry at the gap’s top are nearly the same order, and the gap is the evidence the displacement was real.
The dashed $$$ beside the FVG and the rising trendline of lows below. Internal liquidity in the way of the fall: the first magnets price meets on its way to the 4H sell-side.
Why it matters
This slide is the whole model in one frame, and it is why the post says the concepts must work together. The sweep alone is nothing — highs get swept in ranges too. The shift alone is nothing — shifts fail at higher-timeframe zones. But a sweep at the 4H ceiling, a shift with the 4H direction, and a zone left by that shift with an imbalance at its edge: that is a location, a trigger and an invalidation, which is what a plan is. Separately they are labels; together they are an order.
Rule to carry forward
Demand three things before a zone earns an order: a sweep of something that mattered, a shift with the higher timeframe, and an imbalance at the zone’s edge. Two of three is a watch, not a trade.

entries.p: XAU/USD: Sweep, MSS, FVG and OB
entries.h: The tap, the reaction, and the lows going
entries.t:
Chart: The same stylised 15m chart later. Price has mitigated into the pink order block about halfway, a blue corridor marks the fall, and candles drop through it to a flat SSL line at the session lows; one long candle then breaks that line and ends far below it near 01:30. Slide caption: strong bearish reaction from the order block.
Slide 4 of the post — mitigation taps the block about halfway, and the reaction runs through the session lows.
Step 3 · Delivery
The tap, the reaction, and the lows going
What the slide shows
Mitigation into the OB. Price returns to the block and trades about halfway into it. A limit at the near edge fills; a limit deeper fills too, this time.
The reaction. The block holds on the first tap and price turns down from inside it. No second visit, no drift through the top.
The blue corridor. The fall travels through the internals marked on the previous slide — the $$$ and the trendline of lows are taken on the way, as internals are.
The SSL line, then the break. The session lows are reached and then broken by one long candle near 01:30: the 4H sell-side from slide 1, collected.
Why it matters
Two habits visible here. First, the entry was not chased: the zone was drawn at the shift and price was allowed to come to it, which is the difference between a planned risk and a donated one. Second, the target was never the first thing in the way. The internals and the session lows all stood between entry and the 4H sell-side, and the trade was sized to reach the pool, not the first line. Compare the two gold replays on this site, where the first target sat under 1:2 twice: this post targets the liquidity that the higher timeframe named, and that is the version worth copying.
Rule to carry forward
Let the higher timeframe name the target. Internals in the way are magnets on the route, not destinations; size the idea to the pool.

entries.p: XAU/USD: Sweep, MSS, FVG and OB
entries.h: The chain, link by link
entries.t:
Chart: The post's cover board: the same stylised 15m chart with every mark at once. An X at the swept swing high, a dashed protected-high line above it, a shift mark and the pink order block with a grey extension, an MSS label at the shift low, a blue fall corridor from the block down to a flat SSL line at the session lows, and one long candle breaking that line. Title above the chart: XAU/USD, Sweep + MSS + FVG + OB.
Slide 1 of the post — the whole board in one frame: sweep, protected high, shift, OB, MSS, corridor, SSL and the break.
Everything as one
The chain, link by link
4H bearish: two shifts, a lower high, liquidity taken above.
4H sell-side resting below, untouched: the target, named first.
15m rallies into the 4H ceiling and sweeps the swing high (X).
The sweeping candle’s high becomes the protected high: the invalidation.
15m MSS down, with the 4H: the trigger.
The shift leaves an OB with an FVG at its near edge: the zone.
Mitigation taps the block about halfway: the entry.
The fall takes the internals on the way: the route.
The SSL pool is reached and broken: the target, paid.
Read it against the full sequence and every link has a name this site already uses: direction, target, sweep, shift, zone, entry, hold, exit. Read it against the 15m gold replay on this site and it is the same trade told by two different authors: swept highs, a shift with the trend, a zone drawn in calm, liquidity below as the target. The vocabulary differs — OB and FVG here, supply and $$$ there — the sequence does not.
What the slides leave out
No price axis, no stop line, no target line, no size, and no clock on the wait between shift and tap. Those five things are exactly the five a posted breakdown can afford to omit and a live account cannot. When you copy this setup on your own chart, supply them yourself: the numbers, the invalidation, the target, the risk, and the hours you are willing to wait.

entries.p: XAU/USD: Sweep, MSS, FVG and OB
entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit, in names not prices
entries.t:
The order
Entry, stop loss and take profit, in names not prices
| Part | Level | Why there
| Entry | Sell limit at the OB’s near edge, the FVG’s top | The edge of the block and the top of the gap are the same order here. The slide shows the tap going about halfway in, so an order at the edge fills with room to spare.
| Stop | Beyond the protected high | The high of the sweeping candle. A close above it means the sweep failed and the 15m is no longer delivering down. No tighter: the OB’s top sits below it and wicks through block tops are normal.
| Target | The SSL pool at the session lows, then the 4H sell-side below | Named on the 4H before the 15m setup existed. Internals in between are partial-exit candidates at most, never the target.
| Measure | 1:2 minimum, on your own chart | The slides carry no axis, so no reward-to-risk is quoted here. On your chart: if the distance from the OB edge to the SSL pool is under twice the distance from the edge to the protected high, skip it.
| Size | Fixed risk | Whatever the stop distance costs per lot, size it to 0.5–1% of the account. The wider the protected high sits, the smaller the position.
The gap is evidence, not a target
An FVG at the zone’s edge invites two mistakes: entering at the gap’s bottom instead of the block’s edge (a deeper, greedier fill that misses half the taps), and treating the gap as proof the trade cannot fail. Displacement leaves gaps; some zones with gaps still break. The stop does not move because the gap exists.

entries.p: XAU/USD: Sweep, MSS, FVG and OB
entries.h: What the post teaches, and what it cannot
entries.t:
Review
What the post teaches, and what it cannot
What it does well
Direction first: the 4H slide comes before any 15m detail, so the setup is judged in context.
The sweep is of a level that mattered — the swing high under the 4H ceiling — not of any high.
The zone is drawn at the shift and labelled with its reason: “for mitigation”.
The protected high is named, which is the stop level in all but numbers.
The target is higher-timeframe liquidity, not the first line in the way.
What it cannot show
No prices, so no reward-to-risk: the 1:2 test happens on your chart or not at all.
No stop or target lines, so the exact invalidation and exit are inferred from the marks.
No wait time between shift and tap: an hour or a day changes the trade’s character.
No losing version. A posted breakdown shows the chain working; the failed-trade page shows the same chain breaking.
The fifth slide was not sent, so the trade’s close is unseen.
The caption is the point
“The key is knowing how these concepts work together, not just identifying them on a chart.” On this site that sentence has a home: the full sequence page. Identifying is being able to point at an X, an MSS and an OB. Knowing is being able to say which one must print first, which one invalidates the idea, and which one pays for it — in that order, before price arrives.

entries.p: XAU/USD: Sweep, MSS, FVG and OB
entries.h: Run this the same way every session
entries.t:
Repeatable steps
Run this the same way every session
Name the higher-timeframe direction and its untouched liquidity.Shifts and lower highs for the direction; the pool above or below for the target. Write both before looking at the 15m.
Wait for the 15m to sweep something that mattered in that direction.A swing high for a short into 4H bearish. A random high in a range is not it.
Mark the protected point of the sweeping candle.That is the stop level. If it is too far for 1:2 to the pool, the setup is already dead.
Wait for the shift with the higher timeframe.MSS down for a short. No shift, no zone, no order.
Draw the zone the shift left, and check for an imbalance at its edge.OB plus FVG. The gap is the evidence the displacement was real.
Place the order at the near edge, stop beyond the protected point, target at the pool.One order, three numbers, fixed risk. Then close the chart and let the alert work.
Hold through the internals; exit at the pool or on the invalidation.Internals taken on the way are the trade working, not a reason to move the stop.
Record it: the chain, the numbers, the wait, the outcome.Wins and losses alike. The chain is only as good as the log that tests it.

When to skip
The same setup, refused
Do not take it if
The higher timeframe is flat or pointed the other way.
The sweep took a level nobody was resting behind.
The shift came without an imbalance at the zone’s edge.
The protected point to the pool pays under 1:2.
The zone has already been mitigated once in the session.
This setup had
A 4H bearish structure with its buy-side already swept.
A 15m sweep of the swing high at that ceiling.
A shift with the 4H, leaving OB and FVG together.
A named protected high as the invalidation.
A higher-timeframe pool as the target, and price paying it.
Keep this in proportion
One posted winner, stylised, axis stripped, losing versions not included. It is a clean illustration of the sequence this site teaches, and illustrations are for learning, not for evidence. The evidence you are building is your own log: fifty setups, skips and losses counted, on one pair.
